proof_attempt_summary: D0 proved a universal finite-sample bracket, a sharp growing-arm rate for d <= K^(1-rho), the d=2 case, and saturation corollaries. Primary-source verification corrected the Cai–Low locator to Lemma 1 and attested both cited lower-bound leaves. D0.5 found that the promised closed joint frontier for unsaturated d comparable to or larger than K remains open; closing it needs a common growing-K ratio-max estimator with factorial-variance control and a matching normalized varying-mass lower prior.
tldr: Under consistency, finite-treatment weak unconfoundedness, and the separately maintained balanced-allocation envelope, the causal optimal personalized value is identified by the observed optimal-regression functional. The proved universal finite-sample bracket combines three legal lower bounds with the split-sample plug-in upper bound. It is sharp for every fixed \(\rho\in(0,1)\) throughout \(2\leq d\leq K^{1-\rho}\), where the minimax squared-error risk is of order \(\min\{1,Kd\ell_K/n\}\); the \(d=2\) conclusion holds for every admitted finite \(K\). The bracket also gives order-one risk whenever \(n\leq d/\ell_d\) or \(n\leq Kd\log(1+K/d)\). Only the common ratio-maximum approximation--factorial-variance certificate and its matching normalized moment dual remain open for the unsaturated regime with \(d\) comparable to or larger than \(K\).
gap: The binary frontier fixes treatment count. Published many-arm theory assumes linear context structure or controlled moments, while large-alphabet cusp theory has two normalized distributions and no unknown arm denominators.
fill: The project fixes the completed experiment \(\mathbb P^B\), states the reductions and bracket components as proof obligations, and supplies an exact \((3,2)\) normalized-mixture and heavy--light construction before posing the common polynomial and normalized dual as the first-class open question. Success yields one closed rate, one finite estimator, and one all-estimator converse over the identical model.
